findings.message: us-official-new-york-penn is one reviewed complex but the package still ships it as 4 station ids: us-official-penn (7 calls), us-official-ny-moynihan-train-hall-at-penn (14 calls), us-official-34-st-penn (3 calls)
findings.evidence: The block between 7th and 8th Avenues at 33rd Street. This registry already asserts the core of it: the `us-official-new-york-penn` stationSplitExceptions entry names MTA parents 128 (1/2/3) and A28 (A/C/E) and NJ Transit stop 105 as one complex on MTA's own transfers.txt. The build realised only part of that -- A28 came out as its own id 178 m away -- and LIRR's Penn Station platforms and Amtrak's Moynihan Train Hall concourse, which is Penn Station's Amtrak hall across 8th Avenue and ticketed as NYP, came out as two more. `us-official-penn` is entered here for its New York members ONLY; its ninth member, NJ Transit's 'PENN Station Light RAIL Departure', is a slug collision sitting at Newark Penn 14.4 km away and is excluded by `center`/`maxMeters` (it is claimed by the us-official-newark entry below, which is where the registry's own `us-official-penn` evidence already puts it).

findings.message: us-official-newark is one reviewed complex but the package still ships it as 2 station ids: us-official-penn (1 call)
findings.evidence: Newark Penn Station. Required to finish the New York Penn repair rather than leave a platform stranded: this registry's own `us-official-penn` stationSplitExceptions entry records that NJ Transit's official GTFS publishes rail stop 107 with light-rail stops 26326/42545 as Newark Penn Station, but the build put the rail stop in `us-official-newark` with Amtrak and PATH and left the Newark Light Rail platform in `us-official-penn`, 54 m away and sharing an id with New York Penn. This entry claims that platform for the station the registry already says it belongs to.

findings.message: us-official-washington-union is one reviewed complex but the package still ships it as 3 station ids: us-official-union-marc-washington (3 calls), us-official-union-metrorail (1 call)
findings.evidence: One building on Massachusetts Avenue NE. Amtrak's Washington Union Station (WAS) and MARC's Penn, Camden and Brunswick line platforms are the same train shed and the same tracks; WMATA's Union Station Metrorail (Red Line) is under the station's own plaza with an in-station connection, and WMATA lists it as the Union Station stop. The three arrive as three package ids only because Amtrak, Maryland MTA and WMATA publish three unrelated stop vocabularies, so neither of group_stations' rules can join them: the anchors are 181-260 m apart, past the 140 m name-blind merge, and the three published names ('Washington Union Station', 'UNION STATION MARC Washington', 'Union Station Metrorail Station') do not normalise equal, so the 400 m same-name rule cannot fire either.
